text: Imagine your king tells you to pack up your whole house, and walk eleven hundred kilometres.
It's thirteen twenty seven. Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq rules India from Delhi.
But he has a problem. Delhi is too close to the Mongols, and too far from the south.
So he picks a new capital. Devagiri, deep in the Deccan. He renames it Daulatabad.
And he doesn't just move his court.
He orders the entire city of Delhi to move.
Nobles, soldiers, merchants, scholars, families. Everyone.
He builds a royal road, plants trees along it, and puts rest houses every two miles.
But it's a forty day march, in burning heat.
People get sick. Many never make it.
Delhi becomes a ghost town. One story says only a blind man was left behind.
And Daulatabad? It's too far from the north. The Sultan can't control his empire from there.
So after a few years, he makes a new announcement.
Same road. Same heat. Same forty days.
That's why, seven hundred years later, people still call him the wise fool.
A man with brilliant ideas, and terrible timing.
